question: Do accessible historical Lake Manguao studies and current taxonomic references resolve the endemic minnow and catfish leads well enough for Bangwit species or occurrence records?

sourcesReviewed.citation: Matillano, J. D. (2002). The ichthyofauna of Lake Manguao, Taytay, Palawan, Philippines. Annals of Tropical Research, 24(2), 23-45.
sourcesReviewed.access: The journal article landing page and full abstract were reviewed; the article body and any item-specific reuse terms were not verified.

reportedScope.reportedSampling: The abstract reports two sample events, June and September 2002, six types of fishing gear, eight stations across littoral and open-water zones, and 11 fish species.
sourceReportedTaxa: Puntius bantolanensis and Puntius manguaoensis (historical source usage; not reconciled to current taxonomy)
reportedScope.interpretation: The abstract says both Puntius names and the historical catfish name were collected, but does not expose a station-by-taxon table, specimen identifiers, or coordinates.

limits: Abstract-only access does not establish complete methods, vouchers, exact stations, or a reproducible taxon list.
The article's reported 11-species total differs from Matillano's 2005 SEAFDEC proceedings abstract; the difference is unresolved.
Historical name strings are not current accepted-name determinations or new identifications.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Matillano, J. D. (2005). The ichthyofauna of Lake Manguao, Taytay, Palawan, Philippines with special reference to endemic species. In Proceedings of the First National Congress on Philippine Lakes, pp. 83-100. SEARCA.
sourcesReviewed.access: SEAFDEC/AQD repository metadata and abstract reviewed. The repository states the publication is still for sale in print and its library is restricted from sending the PDF; no purchase or request was made.

reportedScope.reportedSampling: The abstract describes three sampling events in June, September, and November 2002, seven gear types, eight stations, and 12 fish species.
sourceReportedTaxa: Puntius sp. (described in the abstract as a possibly undescribed lake-endemic cyprinid)
Penesilurus palavanensis as a historical synonym of Hito taytayensis in the source's discussion
reportedScope.reportedHistoricalInterpretation: The abstract says the collection supported the historical view that two endemic Puntius species occur in the lake. This is recorded as the paper's interpretation, not as current accepted taxonomy.

limits: The full conference paper was unavailable without purchase; the abstract cannot resolve why its counts and sampling schedule differ from the 2002 journal abstract.
No voucher list, station-level taxon crosswalk, coordinates, or item-specific open reuse license was reviewed.
The 2002 article and 2005 proceedings paper may represent versions of the same survey campaign; do not count them as independent surveys or duplicate their reported effort.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Matillano, J. D. (2011). Taxonomy and conservation of the minnow genus Puntius (Pisces: Cyprinidae) from Northern Palawan, Philippines. MS thesis, SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry, 67 pp.
sourcesReviewed.access: The official SUNY ESF repository record labels the thesis open access and exposes its abstract and bibliographic metadata. Search-indexed thesis excerpts were consulted for the taxonomic-account and habitat-association passages, but the indexed PDF URL was expired and returned 403; the complete PDF was not retrieved or reviewed. The thesis states © 2011, J. D. Matillano, all rights reserved.

reportedScope.abstractScope: The abstract says morphology was analyzed for fish from six northern Palawan drainage basins and reports two endemic Puntius species in Lake Manguao, plus two potentially new species within the basin.
indexedExcerptFindings: The thesis treats Puntius bantolanensis and Puntius manguaoensis as two previously described Lake Manguao species in its historical account.

It describes two additional Puntius morphotypes from the lake basin, one from the lake and one from an inflow, and explicitly defers final taxonomic conclusions pending comparative work and molecular study.
An indexed habitat-association excerpt attributes littoral versus open-water separation to the earlier 2002 survey; this is not adopted as a current species-level ecology or bait claim.

limits: The thesis was not reviewed cover to cover; indexed excerpts do not substitute for checking its complete methods, specimen tables, station coordinates, or rights terms.
The 2011 source's two-species naming predates the current Catalog of Fishes crosswalk that treats the bantolanensis name as a synonym of Barbodes manguaoensis.
The thesis's unresolved morphotypes cannot be matched to the unnamed Barbodes pictured in the 2026 Nagao report by genus, lake, or appearance alone.

sourcesReviewed.citation: California Academy of Sciences, Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes. Online version updated 13 August 2026; entries for Barbus bantolanensis and Barbus manguaoensis.
sourcesReviewed.access: Both current Catalog of Fishes name records reviewed from the official Cal Academy pages.

reportedScope.currentNameCrosswalk: The Catalog lists Barbus bantolanensis as a synonym of valid Barbodes manguaoensis (Day, 1914), with Lake Manguao near Taytay as the type locality for both historical names.
reportedScope.interpretation: This is a current nomenclatural crosswalk, not re-identification of any historical or 2026 specimens and not evidence of a present-day catch at a particular station.

limits: A synonymy record does not resolve the thesis's biological interpretation or identify the two unnamed morphotypes.
Catalog name status and type locality cannot be converted into current presence, abundance, catchability, diet, or a mapped app occurrence.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Balisco, R. A. T. and Liao, T.-Y. (2025). An annotated checklist of fish species described from the Philippines. ZooKeys 1246:1-287.
sourcesReviewed.access: Reused the previously reviewed open-access article-body and publisher XML source entry; the Lake Manguao crosswalk is limited to its historical type-material treatment.

reportedScope.currentNameCrosswalk: The checklist treats Barbus bantolanensis as Barbodes manguaoensis and lists historical type material from Lake Manguao; it is a nomenclatural/type-locality treatment rather than a modern survey.

limits: Historical type-locality material is not a present-day survey record.
The article's separate ODbL supplementary species list was not used for this review.

crossSourceAssessment.surveyVersionConflict: The 2002 journal abstract reports 11 species, June and September sampling, and six gears; the 2005 SEAFDEC abstract reports 12 species, June, September, and November, and seven gears. Both report eight stations and a 2002 Lake Manguao survey. Their relationship may be revised or expanded reporting of the same campaign, but the unavailable full texts prevent resolution. Treat them as one unresolved historical campaign, not two independent surveys.
crossSourceAssessment.taxonomicCrosswalk: The 2011 thesis records two then-current Puntius names and two additional unresolved morphotypes. The current Cal Academy catalog and the previously reviewed 2025 Philippine type checklist treat the bantolanensis name as a synonym of Barbodes manguaoensis. Preserve the thesis's historical usage as source text; use current taxonomy only as a nomenclatural crosswalk, and do not claim specimen re-identification or a resolved biological count.
crossSourceAssessment.siluridNameCrosswalk: The 2002/2005 abstracts use Penesilurus palavanensis and Hito taytayensis in their historical Lake Manguao discussion. The 2025 type checklist maps Penesilurus palavanensis to Pterocryptis taytayensis and records historical type material from Lake Manguao. This supports a name-history crosswalk, not a present-day lake occurrence or an identity for the 2026 Nagao report's unsited Pterocryptis claim.
crossSourceAssessment.palawan2026Connection: The 2026 Nagao report's unnamed Barbodes observations are not reconciled with the 2011 thesis morphotypes or historical named taxa. No specimen, station, date, or image crosswalk supports a match.
crossSourceAssessment.habitats: This batch concerns the inland freshwater lake. It does not add adjacent streams, estuaries, or marine records; those require separate site-level evidence.
crossSourceAssessment.appReadiness: Research-only. The abstracts lack a complete taxon-by-station voucher table and exact stations; the 2011 thesis PDF was not fully retrieved; rights remain unresolved for source-derived content. No present-day fish presence, absence, abundance, diet, bait suitability, safety, legal access, or fishing rule is approved.

rightsReview.status: No source-specific public-app reuse approval was established. The 2011 repository record says open access but the thesis itself carries an all-rights-reserved notice; the SEAFDEC paper remains for sale and unavailable as a PDF; the 2002 full text/license was not reviewed. The 2025 ZooKeys article's CC BY 4.0 source status remains limited to the previously reviewed article body.
rightsReview.handling: No paper, thesis, image, figure, table, or occurrence dataset was retained or copied into the repository.

disposition.reason: Survey-version counts and sampling details conflict, historical Puntius names do not align cleanly with current synonymy, the thesis was available only through metadata and indexed excerpts during this review, and no station/voucher crosswalk or reuse approval supports public records.

nextAction: Continue the Luzon freshwater sequence by checking whether WPU/Palawan museum or collection catalogs expose voucher-level Lake Manguao material for the named Barbodes and unresolved 2011 morphotypes. Keep taxonomy, historical occurrence, modern survey results, and market samples as separate evidence classes; proceed to another Luzon lake or river without claiming Palawan coverage complete.

sources.supports: 2002 journal-article metadata and abstract, including sampling dates, gear/station counts, and the reported 11-species total.
2005 proceedings-paper metadata and abstract, including the 12-species total, three reported sample events, seven gear types, eight stations, and the repository's print-sale/PDF restriction notice.
Official SUNY ESF thesis record, access label, abstract, author/title/year/page metadata; the complete PDF was not retrieved in this review.
Current Catalog of Fishes status of Barbus bantolanensis as a synonym of Barbodes manguaoensis and historical type locality.
Current Catalog of Fishes record for Barbodes manguaoensis as valid and its Lake Manguao type locality.
Previously reviewed 2025 ZooKeys article-body treatment cross-checking historical Lake Manguao type-name relationships for Barbodes and Pterocryptis; not used as a modern ecological survey.
Previously reviewed 2026 short non-comprehensive Palawan report; its unnamed Barbodes observations cannot be matched to the historical thesis morphotypes.
